explanation: Rulers of Kush, Egypt's southern neighbour, were buried under steep, narrow pyramids. Sudan has about 200 or more, against roughly 120 to 140 in Egypt.

claims.text: Sudan has more ancient pyramids than Egypt.
The kings and queens of Kush, in what is modern Sudan, were buried under steep, narrow pyramids.
Sudan has about 200 or more ancient pyramids.
Egypt has roughly 120 to 140 known ancient pyramids.

writerNotes: Self-check (CONTENT_GUIDE §9.3). lint: content:check reports no errors or warnings for this item. claims: every checkable statement is listed; each claim with a digit, number word, superlative, 'first', 'only', quotation or etymology is high (the C26 floor), and so is the key of a counterintuitive item. datasets: no pinned dataset covers these facts (the manifest has no history source), so checker A needs web evidence for every high-risk claim. rivalTest: the argument against the key is that counts depend on what is called a pyramid (Egypt's include ruined and satellite pyramids); every count I know still puts Sudan well ahead, so c3 and c4 are written as ranges at the precision ladder's 'about' rung. volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: the people and events here are reported in world history teaching and reference works, so a player in Lagos, Mumbai, Toronto or Sydney starts level with one in London or Chicago. style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes; the explanation has 25 words. myths: screened every claim against content/reference/myths.json; no claim resembles a listed myth. mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice true/false item. doubts: Counts can grow with new finds, but nothing plausible closes a gap of about 60 to 100, so I set evergreen; the editor may prefer slow. Hard because most people will say false.
